decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Safe vehicle operation requires instruction and practice; a driver manual alone ____.
cards.back: Safe vehicle operation requires instruction and practice; a driver manual alone cannot teach the necessary skills.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Before driving, adjust the seat and mirrors, use restraints, inspect the vehicle, clear ____.
cards.back: Before driving, adjust the seat and mirrors, use restraints, inspect the vehicle, clear the view and secure carried items.
cards.memory_hook: the view and secure carried items

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Trip planning includes deciding whether a trip is necessary and whether a shared ride ____.
cards.back: Trip planning includes deciding whether a trip is necessary and whether a shared ride or public transport can replace driving.
cards.memory_hook: or public transport can replace driving

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Avoiding heavy-traffic periods reduces strain and ____.
cards.back: Avoiding heavy-traffic periods reduces strain and vehicle wear.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Use carpools or shared rides ____.
cards.back: Use carpools or shared rides when practical.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Combine errands by planning destinations and tasks to ____.
cards.back: Combine errands by planning destinations and tasks to reduce separate trips.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Call ahead to confirm needed goods or pickups ____.
cards.back: Call ahead to confirm needed goods or pickups are ready before traveling.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Drivers are responsible for ensuring their vehicles are ____.
cards.back: Drivers are responsible for ensuring their vehicles are safe to operate.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Follow the vehicle owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using a qualified mechanic ____.
cards.back: Follow the vehicle owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using a qualified mechanic for work that requires one.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Have brakes checked by a mechanic if they seem ineffective, make unusual noise, smell abnormal or allow the ____.
cards.back: Have brakes checked by a mechanic if they seem ineffective, make unusual noise, smell abnormal or allow the pedal to sink to the floor.
cards.memory_hook: pedal to sink to the floor

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Check headlights, taillights, brake lamps and turn signals for operation ____.
cards.back: Check headlights, taillights, brake lamps and turn signals for operation from outside the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Brake lights communicate stopping and turn signals communicate turning ____.
cards.back: Brake lights communicate stopping and turn signals communicate turning to other road users.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Misaligned headlights can dazzle other drivers; persistent headlight flashes from others or poor ____.
cards.back: Misaligned headlights can dazzle other drivers; persistent headlight flashes from others or poor night visibility warrant a mechanic’s check.
cards.memory_hook: night visibility warrant a mechanic’s check

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Replace damaged windshield glass because it can break more readily in ____.
cards.back: Replace damaged windshield glass because it can break more readily in a minor collision or impact.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Keep every fitted wiper working and replace blades that no ____.
cards.back: Keep every fitted wiper working and replace blades that no longer clear water well.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distances and hinder ____.
cards.back: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distances and hinder turning on wet pavement.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Low pressure or unbalanced tires can accelerate wear, reduce fuel efficiency and ____.
cards.back: Low pressure or unbalanced tires can accelerate wear, reduce fuel efficiency and make steering or stopping harder.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side ____.
cards.back: Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side calls for a mechanic’s inspection.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Worn tires raise the risk of hydroplaning ____.
cards.back: Worn tires raise the risk of hydroplaning and flat tires.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Measure tire pressure with a gauge while the tires are cold and consult the vehicle ____.
cards.back: Measure tire pressure with a gauge while the tires are cold and consult the vehicle owner’s manual for the specified pressure.
cards.memory_hook: owner’s manual for the specified pressure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: In the handbook’s penny tread check, a tire needs replacement if tread does not ____.
cards.back: In the handbook’s penny tread check, a tire needs replacement if tread does not reach Lincoln’s head when inserted head-first.
cards.memory_hook: reach Lincoln’s head when inserted head-first

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Have steering checked if it is hard to turn or fails to ____.
cards.back: Have steering checked if it is hard to turn or fails to respond when the wheel first moves.
cards.memory_hook: respond when the wheel first moves

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Excessive bouncing after bumps or stops, or difficulty controlling the vehicle, ____.
cards.back: Excessive bouncing after bumps or stops, or difficulty controlling the vehicle, calls for a suspension check.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases and carries ____.
cards.back: The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases and carries them to the vehicle’s rear.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Leaking exhaust gases can be fatal inside a vehicle ____.
cards.back: Leaking exhaust gases can be fatal inside a vehicle in a short period.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Never operate an engine inside a ____.
cards.back: Never operate an engine inside a closed garage.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Have the exhaust checked periodically because many leaks ____.
cards.back: Have the exhaust checked periodically because many leaks cannot be heard.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A commercial vehicle using an engine-compression brake needs a continuously functioning muffler meeting ____.
cards.back: A commercial vehicle using an engine-compression brake needs a continuously functioning muffler meeting manufacturer specifications to prevent excessive noise.
cards.memory_hook: manufacturer specifications to prevent excessive noise

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Maintain the engine according to its owner’s manual because poor running can cause power loss, ____.
cards.back: Maintain the engine according to its owner’s manual because poor running can cause power loss, poor starting or stalling in traffic.
cards.memory_hook: poor starting or stalling in traffic

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Secure loose cabin objects so they cannot strike occupants or ____.
cards.back: Secure loose cabin objects so they cannot strike occupants or roll beneath the brake pedal.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Use the horn as a warning ____.
cards.back: Use the horn as a warning to other people.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A load is secure only when it cannot slide, fall or shift ____.
cards.back: A load is secure only when it cannot slide, fall or shift onto the road or become airborne.
cards.memory_hook: onto the road or become airborne

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Tie loads with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly ____.
cards.back: Tie loads with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Cover the whole load with a strong tarp or net, avoid ____.
cards.back: Cover the whole load with a strong tarp or net, avoid overloading and recheck its security.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with a cloth or paper ____.
cards.back: Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with a cloth or paper towel for cleaning when needed.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Keep washer fluid filled and use an antifreeze wash where ____.
cards.back: Keep washer fluid filled and use an antifreeze wash where freezing temperatures are possible.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Clean the inner window surfaces, especially when smoking ____.
cards.back: Clean the inner window surfaces, especially when smoking leaves a film.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Remove snow, ice and frost from every ____.
cards.back: Remove snow, ice and frost from every window before driving.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Do not hang objects from mirrors or crowd the windshield ____.
cards.back: Do not hang objects from mirrors or crowd the windshield with decals that obscure vision.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Keep headlamps, reversing lights, brake lights ____.
cards.back: Keep headlamps, reversing lights, brake lights and taillights clean.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Check and adjust the seat and mirrors ____.
cards.back: Check and adjust the seat and mirrors before moving off.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Set the seat high enough for a clear road view, without impairing steering, and ____.
cards.back: Set the seat high enough for a clear road view, without impairing steering, and about twelve inches from the wheel.
cards.memory_hook: about twelve inches from the wheel

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Set mirrors to show the rear and side-window views; the handbook suggests seeing only the ____.
cards.back: Set mirrors to show the rear and side-window views; the handbook suggests seeing only the vehicle’s side when leaning forward slightly.
cards.memory_hook: vehicle’s side when leaning forward slightly

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Set a day slash night mirror for the time of ____.
cards.back: Set a day slash night mirror for the time of day you are driving.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Adjust the head restraint so it meets the ____.
cards.back: Adjust the head restraint so it meets the back of the head.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Before driving away, fasten your own belt properly and ensure passengers ____.
cards.back: Before driving away, fasten your own belt properly and ensure passengers use belts or child restraints.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: An officer may stop a vehicle upon seeing an occupant who ____.
cards.back: An officer may stop a vehicle upon seeing an occupant who is unrestrained or incorrectly restrained.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Putting a shoulder belt behind the body or under the arm is improper use, can cause serious injury ____.
cards.back: Putting a shoulder belt behind the body or under the arm is improper use, can cause serious injury and can result in a ticket.
cards.memory_hook: and can result in a ticket

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: An automatic shoulder belt must still be used with ____.
cards.back: An automatic shoulder belt must still be used with the lap belt fastened.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A safety belt helps a driver stay behind the steering wheel during a side impact ____.
cards.back: A safety belt helps a driver stay behind the steering wheel during a side impact or abrupt turn and retain control.
cards.memory_hook: or abrupt turn and retain control

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Safety belts remain necessary in an airbag-equipped vehicle because belts and airbags ____.
cards.back: Safety belts remain necessary in an airbag-equipped vehicle because belts and airbags are intended to work together.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The NHTSA and AAP recommendations reproduced in the handbook say children younger than one should ____.
cards.back: The NHTSA and AAP recommendations reproduced in the handbook say children younger than one should always use a rear-facing car seat.
cards.memory_hook: always use a rear-facing car seat

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Infant-only seats are rear-facing; convertible and all-in-one seats commonly allow rear-facing ____.
cards.back: Infant-only seats are rear-facing; convertible and all-in-one seats commonly allow rear-facing use to higher size limits.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For ages one through three, the reproduced recommendation keeps a child rear-facing until the seat maker’s rear-facing height or weight limit is reached, ____.
cards.back: For ages one through three, the reproduced recommendation keeps a child rear-facing until the seat maker’s rear-facing height or weight limit is reached, then moves to a forward-facing harness.
cards.memory_hook: then moves to a forward-facing harness

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The reproduced recommendation keeps children ages eight through twelve in boosters until an adult belt fits correctly, with ____.
cards.back: The reproduced recommendation keeps children ages eight through twelve in boosters until an adult belt fits correctly, with continued use of the back seat.
cards.memory_hook: continued use of the back seat

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Correct belt fit places a snug lap belt on the upper thighs, not the abdomen, and a snug shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest ____.
cards.back: Correct belt fit places a snug lap belt on the upper thighs, not the abdomen, and a snug shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest rather than the face or neck.
cards.memory_hook: rather than the face or neck

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Choose a car seat that fits both the child and vehicle and ____.
cards.back: Choose a car seat that fits both the child and vehicle and can be used correctly every time.
cards.memory_hook: can be used correctly every time

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Never put a rear-facing child seat ahead of ____.
cards.back: Never put a rear-facing child seat ahead of an active frontal airbag.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A harness should be snug enough that excess webbing cannot be ____.
cards.back: A harness should be snug enough that excess webbing cannot be pinched at the child’s collarbone.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Position the harness chest clip level with ____.
cards.back: Position the harness chest clip level with the child’s armpits.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At the belt path, an installed car seat should move no more than one inch forward slash backward ____.
cards.back: At the belt path, an installed car seat should move no more than one inch forward slash backward or side-to-side under moderate checking force.
cards.memory_hook: or side-to-side under moderate checking force

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Use the top tether whenever possible for forward-facing installation, whether using lower ____.
cards.back: Use the top tether whenever possible for forward-facing installation, whether using lower anchors or the vehicle belt.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Never carry an unrestrained child on your lap; use ____.
cards.back: Never carry an unrestrained child on your lap; use an appropriate child seat.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Read both the vehicle manual and child-seat manual for ____.
cards.back: Read both the vehicle manual and child-seat manual for correct installation and use.

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Do not leave children or animals alone in ____.
cards.back: Do not leave children or animals alone in a hot vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A belt can help prevent being knocked unconscious in a crash, which can ____.
cards.back: A belt can help prevent being knocked unconscious in a crash, which can improve the chance of escaping afterward.
cards.memory_hook: improve the chance of escaping afterward

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Safety belts help prevent ejection into ____.
cards.back: Safety belts help prevent ejection into another vehicle’s path.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: In a side impact, unrestrained occupants can slide toward the impact point ____.
cards.back: In a side impact, unrestrained occupants can slide toward the impact point rather than away from it.

decks.module: Recognizing and responding to traffic stops
decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: An officer can initiate a traffic stop with visible or audible signals such as emergency lights or a siren ____.
cards.back: An officer can initiate a traffic stop with visible or audible signals such as emergency lights or a siren and may approach from either side.
cards.memory_hook: and may approach from either side

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: During a traffic stop, the officer may identify themself and their agency and ____.
cards.back: During a traffic stop, the officer may identify themself and their agency and state the reason for the stop.
cards.memory_hook: state the reason for the stop

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The officer will request the driver’s license, insurance proof and ____.
cards.back: The officer will request the driver’s license, insurance proof and registration during a traffic stop.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Driver and passengers should stay inside the vehicle unless ____.
cards.back: Driver and passengers should stay inside the vehicle unless the officer instructs otherwise.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: When emergency lights appear behind you, remain calm, signal and pull off or aside as soon as safely possible, ____.
cards.back: When emergency lights appear behind you, remain calm, signal and pull off or aside as soon as safely possible, using the right side when possible.
cards.memory_hook: using the right side when possible

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: After stopping for the officer, switch off the ignition and radio, stay inside unless told to exit and keep ____.
cards.back: After stopping for the officer, switch off the ignition and radio, stay inside unless told to exit and keep the hands visible on the wheel.
cards.memory_hook: the hands visible on the wheel

decks.domain: Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: During the stop, remain attentive, avoid mobile-device use and sudden movements, and wait ____.
cards.back: During the stop, remain attentive, avoid mobile-device use and sudden movements, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents.
cards.memory_hook: for instructions before reaching for documents

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Inform the officer at first contact if weapons are ____.
cards.back: Inform the officer at first contact if weapons are present in the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At night, the officer may shine a spotlight ____.
cards.back: At night, the officer may shine a spotlight toward the stopped vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a compliment or complaint about an officer, contact the officer’s agency ____.
cards.back: For a compliment or complaint about an officer, contact the officer’s agency using that agency’s stated channels.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Consult the owner’s manual for starting and apply the parking ____.
cards.back: Consult the owner’s manual for starting and apply the parking brake before starting the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For starting a manual-transmission vehicle, select neutral; some vehicles also ____.
cards.back: For starting a manual-transmission vehicle, select neutral; some vehicles also require depressing the clutch.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, ____.
cards.back: For starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, select Park.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Accelerate smoothly and gradually because an abrupt start can spin the driven wheels and cause ____.
cards.back: Accelerate smoothly and gradually because an abrupt start can spin the driven wheels and cause a slide, especially on slippery pavement.
cards.memory_hook: a slide, especially on slippery pavement

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Practice coordinating the clutch and accelerator so a manual-shift engine does not ____.
cards.back: Practice coordinating the clutch and accelerator so a manual-shift engine does not stall or over-rev during shifts.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Hold the steering wheel with hands on opposite sides, with the left between eight and ten o’clock and ____.
cards.back: Hold the steering wheel with hands on opposite sides, with the left between eight and ten o’clock and the right between two and four.
cards.memory_hook: the right between two and four

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Look well ahead and to both road sides for situations needing steering ____.
cards.back: Look well ahead and to both road sides for situations needing steering so adjustments can be smooth.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The handbook recommends hand-over-hand steering for sharp corners and manually straightening the wheel after the turn rather than ____.
cards.back: The handbook recommends hand-over-hand steering for sharp corners and manually straightening the wheel after the turn rather than letting it slide through the fingers.
cards.memory_hook: letting it slide through the fingers
